caveats_platform: Cell calling is not performed independently for Flex in this release; Cell Ranger's cell calls are used as-is (calibration pending).
The probe set barely covers mitochondrial genes, so the mitochondrial fraction reads low and is not comparable with whole-transcriptome values. A 5% floor is applied to the adaptive threshold.
No public ambient RNA reference range exists for Flex, so contamination is reported as a number without a high/low verdict.
The Flex probe set excludes ribosomal protein, non-coding RNA, TCR/IG and HLA/KIR genes, so its feature universe differs from whole-transcriptome gene expression.

methods.name: Knee and inflection of the barcode rank curve
methods.citation: Lun ATL et al. (2019) EmptyDrops: distinguishing cells from empty droplets in droplet-based single-cell RNA sequencing data. Genome Biology 20:63 (barcodeRanks approach)
methods.license_note: Implemented from the publication; DropletUtils is GPL-3 and its source was not consulted.
methods.description: Unique total counts are collapsed and the log–log curve is differentiated by local quadratic regression. The knee is the point of minimum signed curvature; the inflection is the point of minimum first derivative.
limitations: With an unusual curve shape (for example a double plateau) the knee can land in an unexpected place. The knee is only used as a protective line above which barcodes are called cells directly; it does not by itself determine the cell set.

methods.name: EmptyDrops cell calling
methods.citation: Lun ATL et al. (2019) Genome Biology 20:63
methods.license_note: Implemented from the publication; DropletUtils is GPL-3 and its source was not consulted.
methods.description: Barcodes with total UMI ≤ lower form the ambient profile (Good–Turing smoothed). A Dirichlet-multinomial likelihood is used with α fitted by maximum likelihood; p-values come from a Pólya urn Monte-Carlo simulation, are BH-corrected, and barcodes with FDR ≤ 0.01 are called cells. Barcodes above the knee are retained directly.
params: Cell Ranger cell list used as-is (this assay does not run EmptyDrops)
limitations: The ambient profile depends on the lower threshold. Differences from Cell Ranger come mainly from low-UMI barcodes recovered here; those may be damaged cells or debris and should be read together with the ddqc result.
Monte-Carlo p-value resolution is limited by niters (default 10000).

methods.name: Normalisation / HVG / PCA / kNN / SNN / Leiden clustering
methods.citation: Traag VA, Waltman L, van Eck NJ (2019) From Louvain to Leiden. Scientific Reports 9:5233; Halko N, Martinsson PG, Tropp JA (2011) SIAM Review 53(2) (randomised SVD)
methods.license_note: Implemented from the publications; leidenalg and igraph are GPL and their sources were not consulted.
methods.description: log1p(CP10k) → 2000 highly variable genes by the binned-dispersion method → z-score (clipped at ±10) → randomised SVD to 50 principal components → exact kNN (k = 20) → SNN Jaccard graph → Leiden (RB modularity) at resolution 1.3 (fine, for ddqc) and 0.3 (coarse, for ambient RNA).
limitations: The clustering is only a grouping device for later steps; it is not a cell-type annotation.
kNN uses exact search so that results are bit-reproducible; HNSW approximate search is not used because its layer randomisation cannot be seeded.

methods.name: Ambient RNA estimator A: SoupX-style
methods.citation: Young MD, Behjati S (2020) SoupX removes ambient RNA contamination from droplet-based single-cell RNA sequencing data. GigaScience 9(12)
methods.license_note: Implemented from the publication; SoupX is GPL-2 and its source was not consulted.
methods.description: Empty-droplet counts are summed and normalised into an ambient profile. Cluster-specific marker genes are found by tf-idf. In clusters that do not express a marker, its observed counts are treated as contamination; a Poisson upper-tail test (BH) removes pairs that look like genuine expression. The contamination fraction ρ is then the mode of the conjugate Gamma posterior, iterated until self-consistent.
limitations: It estimates contamination that matches the empty-droplet profile and depends on marker genes being abundant enough in the ambient pool; with few markers the estimate is unstable.
The output is a sample-wide ρ (as in SoupX by default) and does not describe cell-to-cell variation in contamination.
If the mode reaches the edge of the search range the estimate is flagged unreliable and excluded from the consistency verdict.

methods.name: Ambient RNA estimator B: DecontX (background mode)
methods.citation: Yang S et al. (2020) Decontamination of ambient RNA in single-cell RNA-seq with DecontX. Genome Biology 21:57
methods.license_note: Implemented from the publication; celda is MIT-licensed and no code was copied.
methods.description: Each cell's counts are modelled as a mixture of a cluster-native distribution and an ambient distribution; in background mode the ambient distribution is fixed to the empty-droplet profile. Mean-field variational EM estimates the native proportion θ per cell, and ρ = 1 − θ.
limitations: It is conservative for transcriptionally similar populations (shared genes are assigned to the native component); housekeeping genes are mostly called native.
Results are sensitive to clustering granularity: clusters that are too fine underestimate contamination, clusters that are too coarse overestimate it.
This implementation correlates with celda at r = 0.99, but its mean is systematically about 4 percentage points lower.

methods.name: Ambient RNA estimator C: mitochondrial method
methods.citation: Caglayan E et al. (2022) Neuronal ambient RNA contamination causes misinterpreted and masked cell types in brain single-nuclei datasets. Neuron 110(24)
methods.description: Nuclei should contain no mitochondrial transcripts, so in single-nucleus data the mitochondrial read fraction divided by the mitochondrial fraction of the ambient profile approximates the contamination fraction.
limitations: Meaningful only for single-nucleus data; when the ambient profile carries little mitochondrial signal the estimate is unstable and is marked unavailable.

methods.name: Ambient RNA consistency verdict and correction recommendation
methods.citation: Wang Q et al. (2024) A systematic assessment of ambient RNA contamination across 68,000 single-cell and single-nucleus samples (reference ranges: single-cell mean 7.79%, single-nucleus 11.80%)
methods.description: A relative difference of 50% or more between the two estimates is treated as disagreement (exempt when both are below 5%, where the relative difference carries no practical meaning). The sample is rated normal / elevated / severe against the assay reference range. Correction is not recommended when the estimators disagree or the rating is severe, and is greyed out below the assay's grey-out threshold.
limitations: The two estimators model different things: the SoupX-style estimator relies on marker genes appearing where they should not, DecontX on decomposing a mixture of native and ambient distributions. Disagreement is common and may reflect clustering resolution, differences in dissociation, or the presence of a population that resembles the ambient profile.
No ambient RNA reference range has been published for the Flex assay, so values are reported without a high/low verdict.

methods.name: Ambient RNA correction (single method, optional)
methods.citation: Young & Behjati (2020) (subtraction); Yang et al. (2020) (expected native counts)
methods.description: SoupX-style: ρ × total UMI ambient counts are removed per cell and distributed over expressed genes according to the ambient profile (integer output). DecontX-style: the expected native counts from the variational EM are written out (non-integer). The two methods are never chained (constraint C8).
limitations: All ambient correction methods bias expression: highly expressed genes are corrected more strongly, lowly expressed genes barely at all.
Independent benchmarks show every method over-corrects on clean data, which is why the default is to diagnose without correcting.

methods.name: Low-quality cell filtering: ddqc (data-driven QC)
methods.citation: Subramanian A et al. (2022) Biology-inspired data-driven quality control for scientific discovery in single-cell transcriptomics. Genome Biology 23:267
methods.license_note: Implemented from the publication; ddqc_R is BSD-3 and the ribosomal regular expression is aligned with it.
methods.description: After a coarse pre-filter (fewer than 100 genes or more than 80% mitochondrial), adaptive thresholds of median ± 2 × MAD are computed inside each fine cluster for each criterion (lower bounds on counts and genes, upper bounds on mitochondrial and ribosomal fraction), with guardrails (gene threshold ≤ 200, mitochondrial threshold ≥ the assay guardrail). Classic fixed thresholds (mitochondrial < 10%, genes > 500) are reported alongside, and in strict mode they also act as hard bounds.
params: Total UMI (lower bound); Gene count (lower bound); Mitochondrial fraction (upper bound)
limitations: Thresholds depend on clustering quality; MAD is unstable in clusters smaller than about 50 cells.

In single-nucleus data the mitochondrial MAD is often zero; a minimum difference of 0.5% avoids removing every cell. The ribosomal criterion is disabled for Flex, whose probe set contains no ribosomal protein genes.
There is no gold standard for QC and every threshold involves a subjective choice. This tool lists which cells were retained that a fixed threshold would have removed, so the choice can be reviewed.

methods.name: Doublet detection A: cxds
methods.citation: Bais AS, Kostka D (2020) scds: computational annotation of doublets in single-cell RNA sequencing data. Bioinformatics 36(4):1150–1158
methods.license_note: Implemented from the publication; scds is MIT-licensed.
methods.description: Counts are binarised and the 500 genes with the largest p(1−p) are kept. For each gene pair, the log P of observing an excess of mutually exclusive expression is computed under a binomial independence model. A cell's score is the sum of −2 log P over the mutually exclusive pairs it co-expresses; the highest-scoring cells are called according to the expected doublet rate.
limitations: Only heterotypic doublets (two different cell types) can be identified; homotypic doublets cannot.

methods.name: Doublet detection B: DoubletFinder
methods.citation: McGinnis CS, Murrow LM, Gartner ZJ (2019) DoubletFinder: Doublet Detection in Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Data Using Artificial Nearest Neighbors. Cell Systems 8(4):329–337
methods.license_note: Implemented from the publication; DoubletFinder is CC0.
methods.description: Artificial doublets are generated by randomly pairing real cells (pN = 0.25). After merging, normalisation and PCA, each real cell's pANN is the proportion of artificial doublets among its k nearest neighbours; pK is chosen by a BCmvn parameter sweep, and the highest-pANN cells are called according to the expected doublet rate. Each sample is processed independently.
limitations: Artificial-doublet pairing is random: with a different seed the original implementation returns doublet sets with a Jaccard index of only 0.4–0.6. This implementation fixes the seed for reproducibility, but per-cell agreement with the original cannot be exact.

There is no consensus method for estimating the expected doublet rate from the data. This tool uses an empirical formula based on the number of cells loaded (and the multiplexing level); the multiplexed-Flex adjustment is heuristic and user-adjustable.

limitations_global: QC has no gold standard and threshold choices are subjective. This report gives the basis for every step and the reason each cell was removed, so the choices can be reviewed.
Ambient RNA correction biases expression (highly expressed genes are corrected more strongly). The two estimators model different things, so disagreement has several possible causes.
DecontX is conservative for similar populations, calls most housekeeping genes native, and is sensitive to clustering granularity.
There is no consensus method for estimating the doublet rate; the multiplexed-Flex adjustment is heuristic.

The Flex assay has no ambient RNA reference range, and its probe set excludes ribosomal protein, ncRNA, TCR/IG and HLA/KIR genes, so its feature universe differs from whole-transcriptome gene expression.

warnings.value: The raw and filtered matrices list different features; QC used the intersection by feature ID.
